To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice deficient in enoyl-Coa hydratase/3-hydroxy acyl-CoA dehydrogenease, an enzyme that is required to convert enoyl-Coas intod-hydroxyacyls, do not show spontaneous peroxisomal proliferation.
the l-PBE gene is dispensable for normal development and metabolism of mice, and that the l-PBEl-PBE−/– double knockout mice will be useful for the study of peroxisomal and PPARα functions.

mice lacking l-PBE exhibit no spontaneous peroxsome proliferation, and that l-PBE−/- mouse hepatocytes show a blunting of perosxome proliferative response when treated with a peroxsome proliferator, as compared with that of wild type mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of peroxisomal l-PBE and its contribution to the regulation of PPARα and peroxisome biogenesis in liver cells.
the elucidation of the role of peroxisomal l-PBE in the metabolism of endogenous ligand(s) of PPARα and in the regulation of PPARα target genes.
the elucidation of the role of the l-PBE gene in the regulation of PPARα activity in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the l-PBE gene does not appear to be involved in the regulation of PPARα.
l-PBE is not involved in the physiological inactivation of endogenously produced PPARα ligand(s) and is dispensable for the regulation of PPARα-dependent gene expression.
l-PBE is dispensable for the physiological regulation and inactivation of endogeneous PPARα ligand(s) and for the maintenance of normal lipid metabolism in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AOX andl-PBE genes are the only two genes that encode proteins required for the metabolic degradation and the physiological inactivation of endogenously formed peroxisome-proliferator ligands.

AOX is the rate-limiting enzyme for the classical fatty acid β- oxidation system and that the absence of l-hydroxy fatty acids, generated by AOX, inl-PBE-deficient mice is compensated for by the d- hydroxy fatty acids, derived from the d- hydroxylase system, to maintain normal fatty acid oxidation.
l-PBE is dispensable for the metabolism of PPARα agonist ligands in vivo, whereas it is indispensable for the peroxisomeproliferative response in hepatocytes in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the absence of l-hydroxyacylcarnitine (l-OHAC) production inl-PBE-deficient hepatocytes is not responsible for the observed blunting of perosixome proliferation in response to peroxisome prolifeartors.
the l-hydroxyl-specific peroxisomalβ-oxidation system is essential to the physiological regulation of PPARα.
l-PBE− mice are a new mouse model that can be used to study the function of PPARα in the absence of peroxisomes.
